title: The Pre-Verbal Focus Slot in Narrative

sections.title: Neutral Order vs. Narrow Focus
sections.content: In a neutral Hungarian sentence, the topic (what the sentence is about) comes first, followed by the comment starting with the verb (frequently carrying a preverb). However, when a speaker wants to highlight a specific constituent as the single piece of new, unexpected, or contrastive information, that element is placed immediately before the finite verb—in the Focus slot.

sections.title: Exhaustive Identification
sections.content: Hungarian pre-verbal focus expresses exhaustive identification ('it was X, and nothing else, that...'). Placing 'a csend' or 'a szeme' right before the verb tells the reader exactly where the psychological weight of the scene rests.

sections.title: Neutral vs. Focused Sentence Structure
rows: It was the train that Ákos was watching.
It was Ákos who watched the train.
A csend árulta el az igazságot.
It was the silence that betrayed the truth.

items.spanish: Nem a szavak, hanem a hirtelen beálló csend árulta el a titkukat.
items.english: It was not the words, but the sudden silence that gave away their secret.

items.spanish: Antónia a zsebkendőjét szorongatta a peronon.
items.english: It was her handkerchief that Antónia was clutching on the platform.

items.spanish: A kimondatlan szavak okozták a legnagyobb feszültséget.
items.english: It was the unspoken words that caused the greatest tension.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Whenever a non-preverb phrase sits immediately before the conjugated verb, read it with contrastive stress—Hungarian prose relies on this position where English uses 'it was X that...' or vocal italics.
